alerts.title: Carbamazepine lowers dolutegravir levels
alerts.message: Uganda guidelines list carbamazepine as interacting with DTG, decreasing DTG levels by 30-70%, and advise using valproic acid instead. Patient started carbamazepine 400 mg twice daily two weeks ago; viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL despite good adherence, consistent with reduced DTG exposure. Carbamazepine toxicity (level 14 mcg/mL, nystagmus, ataxia, tremor) is also present. Poor adherence is an alternative explanation for viraemia but was reportedly good, making the interaction the leading cause.

evidence.recommended_action: Stop carbamazepine and switch to valproic acid per guidelines; repeat viral load after 3 months to confirm resuppression.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatraemia
alerts.message: Patient has carbamazepine level 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic 4-12) with nystagmus, wide-based gait, and tremor, confirming toxicity. Sodium is 128 mmol/L, and carbamazepine is a recognised cause of hyponatraemia, which can worsen neurological symptoms. The clinician's plan to reduce the dose and repeat the level addresses toxicity, but the hyponatraemia is not addressed. Valproate co-prescription may also contribute to tremor and ataxia. Given the DTG interaction, dose reduction alone leaves the interaction problem unresolved.

evidence.recommended_action: Discontinue carbamazepine in favour of valproic acid, correct hyponatraemia, and recheck sodium and neurological symptoms.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load needs enhanced adherence and repeat testing
alerts.message: Guidelines state virological monitoring provides early indication of treatment failure and routine viral load monitoring is annual for adults. Patient's viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL. The clinician's plan does not include the recommended response to a detectable viral load, such as enhanced adherence counselling and a repeat viral load in three months before assessing for treatment failure or genotype testing. The carbamazepine-DTG interaction is the likely driver, so removing carbamazepine plus adherence support should be combined.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence counselling, resolve the drug interaction, and repeat viral load in 3 months; consider genotype testing if still detectable.

alerts.title: Mild ALT elevation on TDF and hepatotoxic drugs
alerts.message: Guidelines advise liver function tests for TDF toxicity and monitoring for liver toxicity with interacting drugs. ALT is 68 U/L, mildly elevated, in a patient on TDF, valproate, and carbamazepine, all potentially hepatotoxic. The elevation is modest and could reflect carbamazepine toxicity or recent illness rather than TDF; no baseline ALT is available for comparison. The plan does not include repeat LFTs or further hepatic assessment.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat LFTs after stopping carbamazepine; if ALT rises further, evaluate TDF and valproate hepatotoxicity per guidelines.
